text:
Mike K: Heads up — noticed a sustained drop in prefix-cache hit-rate after the 09:10 runtime push; dashboard shows ~14% lower hit-rate for a few high-traffic routes and ~1.6M tokens not saved over the last 3h.

Tal R: Is it widespread or specific slices (model/route/tenant)?

Mike K: Mostly two routes: /chat/stream and /realtime/completions. Models: rwd-v3-small and rwd-v3-medium. Tenants: fastpay, coresearch.

analytics-bot: Quick query I ran:
```
SELECT model, route, tenant, AVG(cache_hit) as hit, SUM(tokens_saved) as tokens
FROM prefix_cache_metrics
WHERE ts >= 1832990000
GROUP BY model, route, tenant
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 15;
```
Top hit delta: fastpay / rwd-v3-small / /chat/stream -> hit down 0.21, tokens_saved -940k

deploy-bot: Runtime bundle rwd-runtime:v3.1.2 rolled at 2026-03-18T09:10Z to edge clusters. Kernel scheduler tweaks and a tokenizer normalization landed in that build.

Jon P: I pulled a short perf profile during the degradation window. Highlights:
- KV cache miss ratio jumped ~2.5x.
- Batch histogram skewed: median batch size fell 7->3, tail similar.
- CPU time per token increased ~12% due to more per-request overhead.
Flame snippet:
```
serving_loop -> dispatch_request -> lookup_prefix_cache
    fallback_path -> disk_prefetch
scheduling -> fast_path_dispatch (more small batches)
```

Tal R: Two candidate causes: (A) tokenizer normalization changed token boundaries that feed cache-key derivation; (B) kernel scheduler fast-path now splits batches more aggressively leading to fewer coalesced requests and less cache reuse.

Sara L: Confirmed: tokenizer change removes a trailing zero-width join in some user messages. That shifts tokenization for many short prompts — cache keys are computed from token sequences, so this will invalidate many recent entries.

Mike K: So keys are incompatible. Options: 1) rollback tokenizer change; 2) introduce key-namespace versioning and support dual-key lookup (try legacy then new); 3) proactively run a backfill/warmup to populate new keys from samples.

Jon P: Rollback is fastest but disruptive if other fixes rely on new tokenizer. Dual-lookup is safer short-term: try legacy_key lookup then new_key, record which version hits. We'll need a metric to track lookup outcome.

Tal R: I'll prototype dual-key lookup in the prefix cache client. Plan: lookup_sequence = [v1_key, v2_key]; emit metric prefix_cache_lookup_attempts{version=..} and prefix_cache_lookup_success{version=..}. Also would like per-tenant warmup_progress gauge.

analytics-bot: Added suggested dashboard panels: prefix_cache_hit_rate_by_key_version, tokens_saved_by_key_version, tenant_warmup_pct. URL: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/Prefetch/prefix-observability (temp panel).

Sara L: For warmup/backfill: we can seed top-K prompt prefixes for affected tenants/models. Idea: sample live incoming prompts for a rolling 24h window, dedupe keys, and run a high-concurrency warmup job to materialize new_key entries in the cache. This avoids long cold-periods.

Mike K: Cost tradeoffs: warmup job will consume tokens to generate prefetched cached responses; but tokens_saved recovery should outweigh warmup cost if we target top traffic slices.

Jon P: Also noted kernel scheduler change reduced micro-batching time window from 7ms->3ms for fast-path. That explains more fragmented batches. We should tune heuristics to allow slightly longer coalescing for routes with high prefix reuse.

Tal R: Agree — will add route-level hints: prefer_coalesce=true for heavy reuse routes. Add a metric: batching_coalesce_delay_ms and batch_size_distribution per-route.

Mike K: Immediate mitigation: deploy dual-key lookup as a non-blocking wrapper to cluster-edges, and kick off warmup jobs for top-10 routes per affected tenant. If hit-rate improves revert wrapper after full migration.

deploy-bot: Scheduled warmup job ids: jw-10021 (fastpay top-10), jw-10022 (coresearch top-8).

Jon P: Added perf notes to ticket PERF-2026: root cause = tokenizer normalization changed token boundaries -> cache key drift -> cold cache -> fewer tokens saved -> scheduler fast-path fragmentation -> higher per-token CPU. Attaching flamegraphs and batch histograms.

Tal R: Also propose a long-term change: make cache key derivation explicitly versioned and stored in a prefix namespace. Keys = hash(version || token_sequence). This avoids silent breakages when tokenization changes. Migration path: dual-lookup then roll forward, then retire legacy after N days.

Sara L: Add alerting: if tokens_saved drops >10% for 20m across core routes -> page oncall; and a low-threshold alert for key_version_mismatch_rate > 5% to notify infra.

Mike K: I'll open PR for dual-lookup and the metrics (prefix_cache_lookup_attempts, prefix_cache_lookup_success, prefix_key_version_mismatch_pct, tenant_warmup_pct). Will also coordinate warmup run and dashboard updates.

Analytics-bot: Tracking note: watch tokens_saved delta and recovery slope. If warmup recovers >80% in 2h we can avoid rollback.

Mike K: Let's reconvene in 45m. If no meaningful recovery we'll rollback tokenizer.

deploy-bot: Dual-lookup canary will be deployed to edge-cluster-2 with sampling=5% at 2026-03-18T10:05Z.

Jon P: Closing loop — will update PERF-2026 with the attached profiles and a timeline.
